## Squachy learns the difference between a pet, a hold, and a pet-pet-pet

The old touch model was one gesture doing three jobs: tapping Squachy pet him *and* changed the background, whether you meant to or not. That's split apart now. The left and right 10% slivers of the screen are dedicated background controls — swap one direction or the other, exactly once per touch, no matter how long you hold. That leaves the middle of the screen free for Squachy himself, who now tells a quick tap apart from a stationary hold apart from an actual petting motion, and reacts differently to each.

AWOK also got its promised smoothness pass: its display was still running at the SPI clock a completely different project's update pattern needed, not this one's every-frame full-screen blit. It's now running at the same 40 MHz the CYD boards already use.

And since none of this is discoverable by staring at the screen, the first-boot walkthrough got a pass to actually explain it — plus a board-specific line, since AWOK has no rotate button to describe in the first place.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added**: left/right 10% edge zones cycle the background one step, fire-once per touch regardless of hold duration
- **Added**: Squachy now distinguishes a tap, a stationary hold, and a dragging pet-stroke, each with its own reactions — only a tap still counts toward the persisted pet-count and milestones
- **Changed**: tapping Squachy no longer also changes the background — that's the edge zones' job now, so you can poke him without redecorating
- **Fixed**: AWOK's display now runs at 40 MHz instead of the inherited 27 MHz, matching the CYD boards — noticeably smoother animation
- **Updated**: the first-boot walkthrough now covers the new edge-zone/gesture controls, with accurate per-board wording (AWOK has no rotate button)
